title: Isabel Spiller teaches him to read music
summary: Miss Isabel Spiller taught him to read and to play with an orchestra, gave concerts at the Lafayette Theatre, and opened his eyes to music; he liked classics but was not deeply interested.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x:
a celebrity and I didn't know anything about it!
Now, at this time I went back to the Henrietta School and met Miss Spiller, Isabel Spiller. She is the one that taught me to really read. Before, anything that the teacher would play, I would just play behind with my ear, you know. But she was the first one that taught me to read, and I became interested in playing with the orchestra. Isabel Spiller. Then I went to her school up on 138th Street. She taught at Rodney School, too, I understand, and at the New School -- and she came from New England Conservatory. This woman was... I didn't know then. I mean, I only know recently, when I look in the... Have you got that book, the Negro Professional book, the artist book...?

Well, she's in there! I called Marion Carbon(?) and he told me about it. I said, 'Did you know Miss Spiller?' He said, 'Did I know Miss Spiller?!' -- and he went into it. I didn't know. Here it is. I've got it somewhere...
But she taught you to play piano legitimately.

Legitimately. And with an orchestra, see. And from then on, for another orchestra... She used to have concerts, give concerts at the Lafayette Theatre with amateur musicians, you know. And she taught all over, you know. She was the one that really started opening up my eyes to music, to take piano ...(?)... (?)... to study. "Hold your fingers high." And I used to think, "Why do I have to..." But the old-time piano players were doing all kind of funny things...
Well, the thing was that they were doing all this for show.
Yeah, yeah, for show, see? And I did like Classics.
